This appendix lists the software packages used or referenced
throughout the course, in the same style as the bibliographic
references. **Julia packages come first** (the workshop's primary
language); **Python packages** follow. Each entry has a one-line
description and a link to the canonical source.

A wider catalogue with commercial offerings and the
residual-loss-PINN-vs-surrogate distinction lives in
[Unit 7 §7.6](../unit_07/unit_07.qmd#sec-software).

## Julia packages

### Core SciML stack — used throughout

::: {#pkg-neuralpde}
**[`NeuralPDE.jl`](https://github.com/SciML/NeuralPDE.jl){target="_blank"}**
— Symbolic PINN solver. Takes a `ModelingToolkit.PDESystem` (equation
+ domain + BCs) and a `PhysicsInformedNN(chain, training_strategy)`
discretisation and builds the physics-informed loss automatically.
The workshop's primary PINN driver.
:::

::: {#pkg-lux}
**[`Lux.jl`](https://lux.csail.mit.edu/stable/){target="_blank"}**
— Explicit-parameter neural-network framework. Keeps parameters
`ps` and state `st` separated from the model so they compose
cleanly with SciML solvers. Used inside `NeuralPDE.jl` for all
network architectures from [Unit 2](../unit_02/unit_02.qmd)
onwards.
:::

::: {#pkg-modelingtoolkit}
**[`ModelingToolkit.jl`](https://github.com/SciML/ModelingToolkit.jl){target="_blank"}**
— Symbolic-numeric CAS. Defines `PDESystem`, the canonical
symbolic-PDE input for both `MethodOfLines.jl` and
`NeuralPDE.jl`.
:::

::: {#pkg-methodoflines}
**[`MethodOfLines.jl`](https://github.com/SciML/MethodOfLines.jl){target="_blank"}**
— Automated finite-difference discretisation of `PDESystem`s.
Used in [Unit 5](../unit_05/unit_05.qmd) and
[Unit 10](../unit_10/unit_10.qmd) to generate FD reference
solutions against which PINNs are benchmarked.
:::

::: {#pkg-ordinarydiffeq}
**[`OrdinaryDiffEq.jl`](https://github.com/SciML/OrdinaryDiffEq.jl){target="_blank"}**
— High-performance ODE/DAE solvers (Tsit5, Rodas5P, QNDF, etc.).
Drives Neural-ODE / UDE training loops in
[Unit 4](../unit_04/unit_04.qmd) and provides ground-truth
trajectories throughout.
:::

::: {#pkg-optimization}
**[`Optimization.jl`](https://docs.sciml.ai/Optimization/stable/){target="_blank"}**
— Unified wrapper over `Optim`, `Optimisers.jl`, `NLopt`, `Ipopt`,
etc. The interface `NeuralPDE.jl` drives for Adam / L-BFGS PINN
training.
:::

::: {#pkg-scimlsensitivity}
**[`SciMLSensitivity.jl`](https://docs.sciml.ai/SciMLSensitivity/stable/){target="_blank"}**
— Forward and adjoint sensitivity backends (`InterpolatingAdjoint`,
`BacksolveAdjoint`, `EnzymeVJP`, `ZygoteVJP`) for differentiating
through ODE / PDE solves inside neural training. Required by the
Neural-ODE / UDE workflow in [Unit 4](../unit_04/unit_04.qmd).
:::

### Automatic differentiation

::: {#pkg-zygote}
**[`Zygote.jl`](https://github.com/FluxML/Zygote.jl){target="_blank"}**
— Reverse-mode source-to-source AD. The default outer-gradient
backend for PINN training in
[Units 5–9](../unit_05/unit_05.qmd).
:::

::: {#pkg-forwarddiff}
**[`ForwardDiff.jl`](https://github.com/JuliaDiff/ForwardDiff.jl){target="_blank"}**
— Forward-mode AD via dual numbers. The default for *inner*
derivatives (spatial / temporal derivatives of the network output)
in PINN residuals.
[Unit 5 §5.2](../unit_05/unit_05.qmd) walks the forward-over-forward
recipe.
:::

::: {#pkg-enzyme}
**[`Enzyme.jl`](https://github.com/EnzymeAD/Enzyme.jl){target="_blank"}**
— LLVM-level AD; increasingly the default in 2025–26 across SciML
(used by `SciMLSensitivity` as `EnzymeVJP`).
:::

### Neural networks and operator learning

::: {#pkg-deepequilibrium}
**[`DeepEquilibriumNetworks.jl`](https://github.com/SciML/DeepEquilibriumNetworks.jl){target="_blank"}**
— Implicit / equilibrium layers built on Lux + DifferentialEquations
with $O(1)$-memory backprop.
:::

::: {#pkg-neuraloperators}
**[`NeuralOperators.jl`](https://github.com/SciML/NeuralOperators.jl){target="_blank"}**
— DeepONet, FNO, Markov NO, NOMAD in Julia. Pairs with
`NeuralPDE.jl` for PINO-style losses; replaces the older
`FluxNeuralOperators.jl`.
:::

::: {#pkg-kolmogorovarnold}
**[`KolmogorovArnold.jl`](https://github.com/vpuri3/KolmogorovArnold.jl){target="_blank"}**
— Lux-compatible KAN layers (radial basis functions, custom
gradients). Introduced in
[Unit 2 §2.7](../unit_02/unit_02.qmd).
:::

### Classical ML and data

::: {#pkg-mlj}
**[`MLJ.jl`](https://github.com/alan-turing-institute/MLJ.jl){target="_blank"}**
— `scikit-learn`-style classical ML framework. Used in
[Unit 2](../unit_02/unit_02.qmd) for the random-forest baseline.
:::

::: {#pkg-decisiontree}
**[`DecisionTree.jl`](https://github.com/JuliaAI/DecisionTree.jl){target="_blank"}**
— Pure-Julia decision-tree and random-forest implementation. The
backend for the MNIST RF demo in
[Unit 2 §2.2](../unit_02/unit_02.qmd).
:::

::: {#pkg-mldatasets}
**[`MLDatasets.jl`](https://github.com/JuliaML/MLDatasets.jl){target="_blank"}**
— Standard ML dataset loaders (MNIST, CIFAR, etc.). Required by
the MNIST examples in [Unit 2](../unit_02/unit_02.qmd); not in
the workshop default `Project.toml` to keep precompile light.
:::

### Plotting and IO

::: {#pkg-plots}
**[`Plots.jl`](https://github.com/JuliaPlots/Plots.jl){target="_blank"}**
— High-level plotting (GR backend by default). Used for all
inline figures.
:::

::: {#pkg-cairomakie}
**[`CairoMakie.jl`](https://github.com/MakieOrg/Makie.jl){target="_blank"}**
— High-quality static figures. Used for the published-quality
plots in [Unit 1](../unit_01/unit_01.qmd) and
[Unit 10](../unit_10/unit_10.qmd).
:::

::: {#pkg-csv}
**[`CSV.jl`](https://github.com/JuliaData/CSV.jl){target="_blank"}**
**+ [`DataFrames.jl`](https://github.com/JuliaData/DataFrames.jl){target="_blank"}**
— Tabular IO. Used throughout for synthetic-mooring data
exchange.
:::

## Python packages

### PINN libraries

::: {#pkg-deepxde}
**[`DeepXDE`](https://github.com/lululxvi/deepxde){target="_blank"}**
— The reference Python PINN library (Lu Lu, originally
Karniadakis group at Brown). Multi-backend (TF1/TF2, PyTorch,
JAX, PaddlePaddle); forward + inverse ODE / PDE / IDE with CSG
geometries. The closest Python analogue to `NeuralPDE.jl`. Used
in [Unit 10 §10.4](../unit_10/unit_10.qmd) for the cross-language
parallel.
:::

::: {#pkg-physicsnemo}
**[`NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/physicsnemo){target="_blank"}**
— PyTorch-based physics-ML framework (formerly *Modulus*). PINNs,
FNOs, MeshGraphNets, diffusion surrogates. The commercial /
production-grade stack catalogued in
[Unit 7 §7.8](../unit_07/unit_07.qmd).
:::

::: {#pkg-physicsnemo-sym}
**[`PhysicsNeMo-Sym`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/physicsnemo-sym){target="_blank"}**
— Symbolic PDE/BC layer on top of PhysicsNeMo (formerly
*Modulus-Sym*); Python analogue of `NeuralPDE.jl`.
:::

::: {#pkg-pina}
**[`PINA`](https://github.com/mathLab/PINA){target="_blank"}**
— PyTorch-Lightning-based PINN + neural operator + PINO library
from mathLab @ SISSA (Rozza group).
:::

::: {#pkg-jinns}
**[`jinns`](https://github.com/mia-jinns/jinns){target="_blank"}**
— JAX-native PINN library (PINNs, SPINNs, HyperPINNs, adaptive
weights) built on Equinox + Optax.
:::

### JAX ecosystem (used in Unit 5 §5.2)

::: {#pkg-diffrax}
**[`Diffrax`](https://github.com/patrick-kidger/diffrax){target="_blank"}**
— Autodiff / GPU ODE / SDE / CDE solvers in JAX (Patrick
Kidger). The JAX counterpart to `OrdinaryDiffEq.jl`.
:::

::: {#pkg-equinox}
**[`Equinox`](https://github.com/patrick-kidger/equinox){target="_blank"}**
— Callable-PyTree neural networks for JAX. Foundation of
`Diffrax` and the typical NN layer for JAX PINNs.
:::

::: {#pkg-flax}
**[`Flax (NNX)`](https://github.com/google/flax){target="_blank"}**
— Google's JAX neural-network library. NNX (2024) is the current
object-oriented API replacing Linen.
:::

### PyTorch ecosystem

::: {#pkg-torchdiffeq}
**[`torchdiffeq`](https://github.com/rtqichen/torchdiffeq){target="_blank"}**
— Differentiable ODE solvers in PyTorch with adjoint backprop.
Standard for Neural-ODE and Burgers-class PINN demos. Used
implicitly in the PyTorch examples of
[Unit 2 §2.6](../unit_02/unit_02.qmd).
:::

::: {#pkg-torchdyn}
**[`torchdyn`](https://github.com/DiffEqML/torchdyn){target="_blank"}**
— PyTorch library dedicated to neural differential equations and
implicit models.
:::

::: {#pkg-pytorch}
**[`PyTorch`](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch){target="_blank"}**
— The deep-learning framework underpinning DeepXDE, PhysicsNeMo,
PINA, torchdiffeq. The MNIST MLP in
[Unit 2 §2.6](../unit_02/unit_02.qmd) is its first appearance.
:::

### Classical ML / data / discovery

::: {#pkg-scikitlearn}
**[`scikit-learn`](https://github.com/scikit-learn/scikit-learn){target="_blank"}**
— The Python classical-ML workhorse. Used in
[Unit 2](../unit_02/unit_02.qmd) for the random-forest, softmax,
and MLP baselines on MNIST.
:::

::: {#pkg-scipy}
**[`SciPy`](https://github.com/scipy/scipy){target="_blank"}**
— Scientific computing routines (`scipy.integrate.solve_ivp`,
`scipy.linalg.svd`). Used in
[Unit 3](../unit_03/unit_03.qmd) for the Python ODE / POD
parallels.
:::

::: {#pkg-numpy}
**[`NumPy`](https://github.com/numpy/numpy){target="_blank"}**
— The Python array library. Foundation of everything else above.
:::

::: {#pkg-pysindy}
**[`PySINDy`](https://github.com/dynamicslab/pysindy){target="_blank"}**
— Sparse identification of nonlinear dynamics (Brunton / Kutz
groups). The Python equivalent of the hand-rolled STLSQ in
[Unit 3 §3.4](../unit_03/unit_03.qmd).
:::

::: {#pkg-pykan}
**[`pykan`](https://github.com/KindXiaoming/pykan){target="_blank"}**
— Reference Kolmogorov-Arnold Network implementation
(Liu et al. 2024). Used in
[Unit 2 §2.7](../unit_02/unit_02.qmd) for the KAN demo.
:::
